Beat 'built' ("So from the eighteen-eighties, the wire went up ... to keep the dingo out"): wrong. Wikipedia's History section (the cited url) says the 1884 fence was a rabbit-proof fence that failed against rabbits; it was heightened and expanded to keep dingoes out later (repurposed around 1914 per other sources; the statewide dingo barrier scheme came after 1948). Fix: e.g. 'In the 1880s it began as a fence against rabbits; as sheep farms spread, it was raised and joined into one wire to keep the dingo out.'

Beats 'loss' -> 'dingo' -> 'built' (fact5, 20,000 sheep a year): misleading chronology and unattributed. The figure is a single PIRSA (South Australian government) spokesperson's estimate of recent losses in South Australia (around 2018, before the modern rebuild closed gaps), not the 1880s motive; the script uses it as the reason the fence was built ('Lost to what? ... So from the eighteen-eighties, the wire went up'). Also 'farmers there' points at the south-east, but the figure is South Australia's. Profile requires a single-source claim to be attributed on screen: say e.g. 'South Australia's government says that before recent gaps were sealed, about 20,000 sheep a year were lost' and place it after the history, or drop it.

Confirmed on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingo_Fence (WebFetch): 5,614 km; 'previous length of over 8000 km' (script says 'over', ok); built 1880-85; 180 cm mesh (mostly); states SA, NSW, Qld; ends at Jimbour (Darling Downs) and on Nullarbor cliffs above the Great Australian Bight; dingoes on the north-western side. Disclaimer ends the description. Style notes: 'cuts the whole continent in two' is a simplification (the fence ends inland at Jimbour); 'The characters are not advisers.' in the description is unneeded on this channel.
